newsitem.title: UK: Belfast man seized with bomb-making equipment.
newsitem.headline: Belfast man seized with bomb-making equipment.

text.p: Police said they detained a man on Friday after seizing bomb-making equipment in the Catholic Markets area of Belfast.
The arrest coincided with stepped-up security by police and troops in Northern Ireland after a suspected Irish Republican Army (IRA) sniper killed a British soldier on Wednesday.
Few details of the arrest were made public. Police patrols in the Markets have come under attack this year after the IRA ended a truce a year ago.
British Prime Minister John Major said the IRA campaign against British rule would not force any concessions from his government.
"We will never be bombed or sniped out of our principles in Northern Ireland or anywhere else," he told reporters during a visit to Wales.
The British government says the IRA must call a permanent end to its 28-year guerrilla war before Sinn Fein, its political wing, can take part in peace talks.
An IRA sniper is thought to have killed the 23-year-old British soldier, who was shot at an army checkpoint in the southern village of Bessbrook.
The killing aroused fears that the IRA's arch-foes, Protestant Loyalists who want the province to stay British, would end their own two-year truce to avenge IRA attacks.

The Combined Loyalist Military Command, the umbrella organisation for the outlawed Loyalist groups, was expected to meet in the next 72 hours to decide its next step, sources close to the organisation said.
The sources declined to speculate whether the Loyalists would hold their fire or decide to launch revenge attacks against Catholic targets.
Police believe Loyalists carried out two attacks against Catholics in recent months but say the CLMC ceasefire is officially still intact.

A 17-person U.S, Congressional fact-finding delegation was due in Belfast on Friday but was delayed by technical trouble to the aircraft carrying them from Shannon, Ireland, to Northern Ireland, officials said.
The delegation will hold luncheon talks with Irish Prime Minister John Bruton in Dublin on Saturday and also meet Britain's Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine.
